title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-05-13
content:
Week: 2026-05-11 to 2026-05-13
Owners: Anya Patel (update author), Marcus Chen, Liam O'Rielly, Priya Menon, Diego Alvarez
Attendees (sync): Anya, Marcus, Liam, Priya, Diego, Sasha (benchmarks), Noor (SRE)

TL;DR
- Kernel micro-optimizations landed in staging (PR #1423) with median token latency improvements of ~8% for long-sequence flows; still seeing a 2-3% regression on short chat traces.
- KV cache prototype evictions/backpressure logic merged to feature branch; initial load-testing shows cache hit-rate improvements from 57% -> 71% on our long-prompt replay suite.
- Batching scheduler v2 (dynamic windowing) is behind schedule; blocked by a correctness bug that causes out-of-order logits when preemption occurs. Patch ETA EOD Friday.

Highlights and progress
1) Kernel work (Marcus + Priya)
  - PR #1423 merged to staging: reduced memory copies in attention kernel for causal masks, implemented vectorized gather for KV offsets on A100/4090 paths.
  - Benchmark summary (staging): long seq (seq_len 4k) median per-token latency: 12.1ms -> 11.1ms (~8% improvement). Short seq (seq_len <128) median per-token latency: 4.2ms -> 4.3ms (+2.4% regression).
  - Investigation plan for short-seq regression: likely branch misprediction overhead introduced by the vectorized path; Priya to run instruction-level profiling (perf + nvprof) across batch sizes and submit follow-up micro-PR to revert the vectorized path when seq_len < 256.
  - Action items: Marcus to open a follow-up PR by 2026-05-15 to add heuristic fallbacks; add unit tests for masked-gather correctness (covering edge cases around padding).

2) KV cache (Liam + Diego)
  - Feature branch: kv-cache-enhanced-eviction merged into feature branch. Key changes: LRU segmentation per-request-id, TTL-based soft-evictions for stale prefixes, and adaptive admission control under memory pressure.
  - Load test results (replay of customer traces, 12h window): hit-rate improved 57% -> 71% (avg tokens saved per request +28%). Overall GPU token throughput increased by ~15% for these workloads.
  - Observability: added per-route KV hit/miss and eviction counters to the debug table; dashboards instrumented in staging console.
  - Known issue: pathological growth of per-request segment counts when many short-lived requests create small prefixes (observed with high-concurrency API tests). Mitigation: Diego implemented a per-request max-segments cap with sampling; needs validation for tail latency impact.
  - Action items: Diego to run a 48h soak with per-request cap and report tail-99 latency; Liam to add an admission-control metric exposing bytes rejected due to memory caps.

3) Batching (Anya + Sasha)
  - Dynamic windowing scheduler (v2) introduced to improve utilization for mixed-latency workloads; introduces adaptive timeouts per-class and sequence-length-aware window expansion.
  - Blocker: non-deterministic ordering when preemption/rescheduling occurs -> causes token alignment mismatch and rare soft-failures in sampled traces. Root cause narrowed to race in token-index assignment during preempt sequence; failing reproducibly under stress harness.
  - Workaround: revert to v1 scheduler for production routes while we iterate on v2. Opt-in flag available in staging.
  - Action items: Anya to land race-fix patch (synchronization + sequence-numbering) by EOD 2026-05-14; Sasha to run stress harness for 24h after patch landing.

Operational notes and metrics
- Deployments: staging has kernel PR + KV feature branch behind feature flag. Canary rollout blocked due to batching regression; do not promote to canary until batching race fixed and 24h stress test passed.
- Perf dashboards (staging): overall token/sec increased by 6% week-over-week mainly due to KV improvements; 95th latency for chat routes increased 4% due to kernel short-seq regression.
- Cost impact estimate: KV improvements projected to reduce GPU token units by ~12% for customers with long-prefix workloads (finance to take a closer look before external comms).

Blockers / Risks
- Kernel short-seq perf regression (+2-3%) could regress SLAs for low-latency chat customers. High priority to add seq_len heuristic and revert vectorized path for tiny sequences.
- Batching v2 race is a hard correctness issue; until fixed we must keep v2 out of canary. This slows overall utilization gains targeting peak hours.
- KV per-request-seg explosion under synthetic high-concurrency could lead to memory blowups in extreme tails; mitigation is in place but needs longer soak.

Decisions made this week
- Keep KV feature behind feature flag for canary until 48h soak with per-request cap finishes.
- Revert production scheduler to v1; continue v2 development in staging behind opt-in.
- Prioritize kernel short-seq heuristic before any canary expansion to prevent customer-facing regressions.

Meeting notes / standup snippets
- 2026-05-11 Standup: Marcus: "kernel PR landed, need profiling for short traces"; Liam: "KV hit-rate looks promising; watch for segment explosion"; Anya: "batching v2 brings deterministic ordering issues, reverting in prod for now".
- 2026-05-12 Sync: Diego demoed KV eviction counters and dashboard; Sasha presented stress harness findings that reproduced batching preemption race at ~20k concurrent requests. Agree to prioritize race fix.
- 2026-05-13 Triage: Decided add per-route opt-out for dynamic batching to allow safe rollout per-customer.

Action items (owners and due dates)
- Marcus: add seq_len <256 heuristic and micro-PR to revert vectorized gather path for short traces (due 2026-05-15).
- Priya: run instruction-level profiling and send perf flamegraphs to kernel@ (due 2026-05-14).
- Anya: land batching race-fix patch and coordinate 24h stress run with Sasha (patch due 2026-05-14, stress run complete by 2026-05-15).
- Diego: run 48h KV soak with per-request cap and report tail-99 latency (start 2026-05-13, report 2026-05-15).
- Liam: add admission-control metric for KV memory rejections and wire to staging dashboards (due 2026-05-16).

Notes / loose thoughts
- Consider adding a micro-benchmark for short-seq chat paths in the CI perf suite so we get early detection of kernel regressions.
- For KV, explore probabilistic admission (TinyLFU-style) in addition to TTL-based soft-evictions for improving hit-rate while bounding memory.
- Product ask: if KV hit-rate stays >70% in canary, product wants to draft an external note about cost/perf wins for targeted customers; coordinate with finance for unit economics.

Relevant links and artifacts
- Kernel PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1423
- Batching patch (staging opt-in): github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1431
- KV design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRV/pages/12345/kv-cache-design
- Stress harness (internal): github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools/tree/main/stress-harness

Next week focus (2026-05-18 sprint)
- Close kernel short-seq regression and add CI micro-benchmark.
- Stabilize batching v2 race and run full 48h stress test.
- Continue KV soak and finalize canary rollout plan based on 48h results.

-- End of update
